question: Your web search subagent retrieves pages through a fetch_url tool. A legal policy forbids retrieving any content from domains on a company blocklist. The system prompt states this rule, yet logs show that the web search subagent still fetched blocked domains in a few runs. What is the most effective way to enforce this policy?

options.text: Instruct the synthesis subagent to review all citations and remove any source that comes from a blocklisted domain.
options.reason: This step relies on prompt instructions and acts after the fetch, so it gives no guaranteed prevention of the forbidden call.

options.text: Add a PostToolUse hook that deletes content from blocklisted domains in each fetch_url result before the web search subagent processes it.
options.reason: PostToolUse hooks transform tool results after the call has run, so the forbidden retrieval has already happened.

options.text: Rewrite the system prompt with emphatic warnings and few-shot examples that show the web search subagent refusing blocklisted domains.
options.reason: Prompt instructions give only probabilistic compliance, and the logs already show that the prompt rule fails in some runs.

options.text: Add a tool call interception hook that checks each outgoing fetch_url call against the blocklist and blocks it before execution.
options.reason: A hook that intercepts outgoing tool calls enforces a compliance rule deterministically, because the blocked fetch never runs.
